title: Interaction Box Attributes
description: Defines the attributes of an interaction box, used for player interaction with parts. An interaction box usually corresponds to bones in the model: when the player aims at (accurate) or touches (fast) it and presses the interact key, the box asks the target subsystems in signal_targets order one by one. What counts is where the box sits in the world, not which part's JSON declares it; the declaring part decides which sub-part's destruction removes the box, and whether the target needs cross-part wiring.

bone.description: Bone name corresponding to the interaction area, bones in the model will serve as the interaction area.

signal_targets.description: Interaction targets: the key is a channel name, the value is a target list. A target is a subsystem name in the same part, or a connector name so the interaction reaches a subsystem on the other part across parts; only subsystems can take over an interaction, any other name is rejected at load time. List order is the order they are tried: a door leading to several seats fills the first free one and an occupied seat only yields without ending the walk. For same-part links the channel name is just a grouping label; across parts it is the arrival channel the opposite connector's table recognises. Targets are resolved into a terminal subsystem list on structure change and when the vehicle enters the level; an unwired cross-part line, or a missing arrival channel on the opposite side, leaves that list empty and the box completely inactive - no prompt, and the aim ray cannot pick it either.

interact_mode.description: Interaction mode. fast: quick interaction, only requires player to intersect with the interaction area; accurate: requires player to aim at the interaction area. Between the two, accurate has higher priority than fast.

condition.description: Gate expression: a MoLang script whose value above 0 means the interaction box is usable right now, evaluated in the host part's local.* and global.* context (subsystem state, signal storage, assembly values). Omit it or write true for no gate. A broken expression does not block loading, but this interaction box stays permanently unusable and leaves an error log.

examples.description: Door handle: direct same-part link to the driver seat
Rear hatch: commander seat first, gunner seat when that one is taken
Trunk lid: opens only with the engine off; across parts write the connector name as the target
